sections.title: 1. Who we are and scope
sections.content:
These terms govern the use of SmileCheck by patients, who are consumers.

SmileCheck is operated by [company name — to be completed], a Portuguese company with registered office at [address — to be completed], tax no. [to be completed]. Contact: {{email}}.

Dentists and clinics have their own terms: “Terms for professionals”.

sections.title: 2. The service
sections.content:
SmileCheck lets you book appointments, talk to professionals, keep oral-health information and take part in a points programme.

SmileCheck does not provide healthcare. Care is provided by dentists and clinics, who are solely responsible for clinical acts. Teleconsultation is not available yet (“Coming soon”).

sections.title: 3. Account and minimum age
sections.content:
You must give accurate details and keep your password secret.

Minimum age to open an account on your own: 13 in Portugal and 15 in France. Below that age, the account is managed by the person with parental responsibility, through a family profile.

sections.title: 4. AI triage
sections.content:
AI triage gives general guidance only. It is not a medical device: it gives no diagnosis, names no disease, does not rate severity and does not recommend treatments or medication.

The result is a summary of the symptoms you entered, to show your dentist, with general hygiene and comfort tips. In an emergency, call 112 (Portugal) or 15 (France). Limited to 10 requests a day.

sections.title: 5. Reviews
sections.content:
You can only leave a review after an appointment that took place between both parties, once per appointment.

How we verify: our server automatically checks that the appointment exists, has ended and involves both the reviewer and the person reviewed; only then is the review accepted and shown as “Verified review”. You can edit it for 24 hours. We may remove unlawful or abusive reviews, or reviews unrelated to the appointment.

sections.title: 6. Points, levels and ads
sections.content:
There are two kinds of points: XP, which sets your level and is never spent, and reward points, which you exchange in the store.

You earn points through actions in the app (for example, attending appointments, leaving reviews, confirmed invites), only with a verified phone. You lose points when you exchange them and through penalties (for example, missing an appointment without notice).

On the Free plan, reward points are reset to zero once a year, with prior notice in the app. On paid plans they are never lost.

Points have no cash value: they cannot be refunded, converted or transferred.

The Free plan shows ads, which never use health data and are only personalised with your consent. 5 videos give 8 ad-free hours; 10 ads give 2 reward points, once a day.

sections.title: 7. Plans, prices and renewal
sections.content:
Free, Pro and Premium plans, monthly or yearly (yearly with 15% off). Prices for patients include VAT.

Payment is handled by Stripe; SmileCheck never sees or stores your card details. Subscriptions renew automatically. For yearly plans, we remind you in the app and by email 30 days before renewal.

sections.title: 8. Right of withdrawal (14 days)
sections.content:
As a consumer you normally have 14 days to withdraw from a distance contract.

When you subscribe to a paid plan, you ask for the service to start immediately and acknowledge that you lose the right of withdrawal once the service has started. We record the date and time of that request.

sections.title: 9. Cancelling your subscription and appointments
sections.content:
You can cancel at any time in Plan › “Cancel subscription” (or in the footer, “Manage/cancel subscription”), in Stripe's secure portal. The plan stays active until the end of the period already paid and is not charged again.

Appointments: cancel at least 24 hours in advance.

sections.title: 10. Deleting your account and downloading your data
sections.content:
In Settings › Security you can download your data (JSON file) and delete your account, with double confirmation. On deletion we cancel your subscriptions and delete or anonymise account data, points, invites, preferences, consents and messages.

The clinical record is not deleted: it stays with the responsible professional, detached from your account, because the law requires it to be kept.

sections.title: 11. Liability
sections.content: We do our best to keep the app available and secure, but interruptions may happen. We are not liable for professionals' clinical acts. Nothing in these terms limits your statutory rights as a consumer.

sections.title: 12. Changes
sections.content: If we change these terms, we will tell you in the app and by email with reasonable notice. If you do not agree, you can delete your account.

sections.title: 1. Controller
sections.content:
SmileCheck — [company name, address and tax no. — to be completed] — is the controller for account data, points, ads, invites, preferences, consents and payments.

Data protection officer (DPO): [name — to be completed]. Contact: {{email}}.

sections.title: 2. Clinical data: who is responsible
sections.content:
The clinical record (notes, allergies entered by the professional, fear assessments made by the professional, prescriptions, referral letters) is the responsibility of the dentist or clinic that keeps it. SmileCheck processes that data as a processor (GDPR article 28), only on the professional's instructions.

You can ask the professional or us for access to your record; if you ask us, we forward the request.

sections.title: 3. Data we process
sections.content:
• Account: name, email, phone, language, date of birth.
• Health (special category data, GDPR article 9): triage answers, allergies, fear self-assessment, appointments.
• Points programme: points, levels, achievements, invites, ads watched (counters).
• Payments: plan and subscription status (card details stay with Stripe).
• Technical: device, security logs and record-access logs.
• Consents and preferences.

sections.title: 4. Purposes and legal bases
sections.content:
• Providing the service and managing the account — performance of the contract.
• Health data — explicit consent and care by professionals bound by secrecy (GDPR article 9(2)(a) and (h)).
• Invoicing — legal obligation.
• Security and abuse prevention — legitimate interest.
• Statistics and personalised ads — only with your consent; refused by default.

sections.title: 5. Processors
sections.content:
• Hosting and database: [provider — to be completed], [country, EU — to be completed].
• Payments: Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd., Ireland (EU).
• Artificial intelligence (triage): [provider — to be confirmed], [country — to be completed]; receives only the symptoms entered, without name or contact details.
• Email: [provider — to be completed], [country — to be completed].

Transfers outside the European Economic Area only with appropriate safeguards (for example, standard contractual clauses). Certified health-data hosting for France (HDS) is under review.

sections.title: 6. Retention
sections.content:
• Account: while it is active.
• When you delete your account: account data, points, invites, preferences, consents and notifications are deleted or anonymised immediately.
• Clinical record: kept by the responsible professional for the legal period [period — to be confirmed per country].
• Invoicing: for the legal tax period [to be confirmed].
• Record-access logs: [period — to be completed].
• AI triage requests: we keep only the time of the request, for the daily limit.

sections.title: 7. Your rights
sections.content:
Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection; you can withdraw consent at any time, without affecting what was done before.

In the app: Settings › Security › “Download my data” and “Delete account”; Settings › Privacy for consents. Other requests: {{email}}. We reply within one month.

sections.title: 8. Complaint to the supervisory authority
sections.content: You can complain to the CNPD (Portugal) — https://www.cnpd.pt — or the CNIL (France) — https://www.cnil.fr.

sections.title: 9. Children
sections.content: Minimum age to consent on your own: 13 in Portugal and 15 in France. Below that, the account is managed by the person with parental responsibility (family profile).

sections.title: 10. Security
sections.content: Encrypted connections, role-based access control, logging of who opens the clinical record and record access only within an active care relationship.

sections.title: 11. Cookies and local storage
sections.content: We only use storage needed for the app to work. Statistics and personalised ads only with your consent, which you can change in Settings › Privacy.

sections.title: 12. Changes
sections.content: If we change this policy, we will tell you in the app and by email.

sections.title: 1. Commitment and reference standard
sections.content: SmileCheck aims for the app to be usable by everyone, in line with the European Accessibility Act. The reference standard is WCAG 2.1 level AA, through the European standard EN 301 549.

sections.title: 2. Compliance status
sections.content: Partially compliant. Some parts do not yet meet every WCAG 2.1 AA requirement (see known limitations). This statement does not claim full compliance.

sections.title: 3. What we have done
sections.content:
• Touch targets of at least 44 × 44 px on phones and tablets.
• AA text contrast in light and dark themes on most screens.
• Accessible names on icon-only buttons, translated into Portuguese, French and English.
• Keyboard navigation with visible focus on the main controls.
• Support for the system “reduce motion” setting.
• Page language and screen titles kept up to date for screen readers.

sections.title: 4. Known limitations
sections.content:
• Appointment-type colours and some level colours are protected identification colours and may have contrast below 4.5:1 on small text.
• Some cards and agenda items are not yet fully keyboard operable.
• The search map has limited accessibility; the list view offers the same information.
• Sample videos have no captions.

sections.title: 5. Report a problem
sections.content: If you find an accessibility barrier, write to {{email}}. Tell us the screen, the device and what happened. We reply within 30 days at most.

sections.title: 6. Last review
sections.content: This statement was reviewed on {{date}}.

sections.title: 1. Scope
sections.content: These terms apply to dentists and clinics using SmileCheck in the course of their business (business-to-business). They complement the Terms of service. Provider: [company name, address and tax no. — to be completed].

sections.title: 2. Verification
sections.content: New accounts stay pending until we verify professional registration (dental council / RPPS) and, for clinics, the operating licence. Only approved accounts appear in search.

sections.title: 3. How search works
sections.content:
Results only show verified professionals matching what the patient looks for: specialty, distance from the address given and availability. Patients can sort by distance (default) or by price.

There is no paid placement: plan, level, points and rankings do not affect the order, and no store reward buys visibility.

sections.title: 4. Rankings, levels and badges
sections.content: Pending the dental council's opinion, each professional's rankings, levels, seals and highlighted achievements are visible only to that professional and their clinic. Patients never see them, neither in search nor on profiles. In leaderboards, other professionals are anonymous.

sections.title: 5. Clinical data
sections.content: The professional is the controller of clinical-record data; SmileCheck is a processor (GDPR article 28) and processes it only on your instructions [data processing agreement — annex to be completed]. Record access requires an active care relationship and is logged. When a patient deletes their account, the record stays with you, detached from the account.

sections.title: 6. Reviews
sections.content: Patients can only review you after an appointment that took place with you, once per appointment; the server automatically checks the appointment before accepting the review (“Verified review”). You can ask for a review to be reconsidered through internal complaints.

sections.title: 7. Points and ads
sections.content: You earn points through actions in the app (appointments, reviews, confirmed invites — only with a verified phone and an approved account) and lose them when you exchange them and through penalties. On the Free plan reward points are reset once a year and ads are shown (no health data). Points have no cash value.

sections.title: 8. Plans, prices and commissions
sections.content: Prices exclude VAT (VAT added at the legal rate). SmileCheck commission on teleconsultations: 15% (Free), 10% (Pro), 5% (Premium) — teleconsultation is not available yet. Dentists per clinic: 2 (Free), 5 (Pro), unlimited (Premium). Automatic renewal; cancellation takes effect at the end of the paid period.

sections.title: 9. Restriction, suspension and termination
sections.content: If we restrict or suspend your account, we email you the reasons in writing, before or when it happens: the facts and the rules applied. You can reply and ask for a review. To end the service we give at least 30 days' notice, unless required by law or for a serious breach.

sections.title: 10. Changes to these terms
sections.content: We notify you by email at least 15 days in advance, stating what changes. If you do not agree, you can terminate before the change takes effect.

sections.title: 11. Internal complaints
sections.content: Free of charge, via {{email}}. We review each complaint and reply in writing within [period — to be completed].

sections.title: 12. Mediation
sections.content: If a complaint does not settle the matter, you can use mediation. Designated mediators: [name and contact of at least two independent mediators — to be completed]. We take part in good faith.

sections.title: 13. Governing law
sections.content: Portuguese law and Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 on online platforms.

fear.title: Fear scale
fear.selfTitle: How do you feel at the dentist?
fear.selfHint: You can change it at any time. It helps the team adapt your appointment.
fear.mismatch: The patient's self-assessment and the clinical assessment differ by 2 or more levels.
fear.panelSubtitle: P = patient's self-assessment · C = clinical assessment
fear.updateHint: The last value is preselected; tap to confirm or pick another.
fear.saveError: Could not save the fear level

0.label: Calm
0.desc: Relaxed and cooperative; understands the procedure.

1.label: Mild apprehension
1.desc: Mild anxiety; asks questions and cooperates.
1.conduct: Explain each step and answer questions.

2.label: Moderate anxiety
2.desc: Visible tension; mild physical signs may appear (e.g. tachycardia).
2.conduct: Calm environment, agreed breaks and frequent comfort checks.

3.label: Intense fear
3.desc: Obvious fear; risk of resisting treatment.
3.conduct: Tell-show-do technique and an agreed stop signal; consider anxiolysis or premedication.

4.label: Panic
4.desc: Anxiety attack or refusal of treatment.
4.conduct: Postpone non-urgent procedures; consider conscious sedation or referral.
